passages.text: Wives, in the same way, submit yourselves to your husbands, so that even if they refuse to believe the word, they will be won over without words by the behavior of their wives when they see your pure and reverent demeanor.
passages.sermon:
Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands.
Do this in the same way as others who follow Christ.
Some husbands do not believe the word of God.
Your behavior can win them over, even without words.
They will see your pure and respectful conduct.
Your reverent life will influence them.
passages.original: Ὁμοίως αἱ γυναῖκες ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν ἵνα καὶ εἴ τινες ἀπειθοῦσιν τῷ λόγῳ διὰ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀναστροφῆς ἄνευ λόγου κερδηθήσονται ἐποπτεύσαντες τὴν ἐν φόβῳ ἁγνὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν

passages.text: Your beauty should not come from outward adornment, such as braided hair or gold jewelry or fine clothes, but from the inner disposition of your heart, the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious in God’s sight.
passages.sermon:
God values true beauty.
True beauty does not come from outward adornment.
Braided hair does not make you truly beautiful.
Gold jewelry does not make you truly beautiful.
Fine clothes do not make you truly beautiful.
True beauty comes from within your heart.
A gentle spirit is truly beautiful.
A quiet spirit is truly beautiful.
This inner beauty does not fade.
God sees this inner beauty.
God considers this inner beauty precious.
passages.original: ὧν ἔστω οὐχ ὁ ἔξωθεν ἐμπλοκῆς τριχῶν καὶ περιθέσεως χρυσίων ἢ ἐνδύσεως ἱματίων κόσμος ἀλλ’ ὁ κρυπτὸς τῆς καρδίας ἄνθρωπος ἐν τῷ ἀφθάρτῳ τοῦ πραέως καὶ ἡσυχίου πνεύματος ὅ ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ πολυτελές

passages.text: For this is how the holy women of the past adorned themselves. They put their hope in God and were submissive to their husbands, just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. And you are her children if you do what is right and refuse to give way to fear.
passages.sermon:
The holy women of the past trusted God.
These women made themselves beautiful by their actions.
They submitted to their own husbands.
Sarah was one of these women.
Sarah obeyed Abraham.
Sarah called Abraham her lord.
You become Sarah’s children when you do what is right.
You must not give in to fear.
passages.original: Οὕτως γάρ ποτε καὶ αἱ ἅγιαι γυναῖκες αἱ ἐλπίζουσαι εἰς Θεὸν ἐκόσμουν ἑαυτάς ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν ὡς Σάρρα ὑπήκουσεν τῷ Ἀβραάμ κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα ἧς ἐγενήθητε τέκνα ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι καὶ μὴ φοβούμεναι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν

passages.text: Husbands, in the same way, treat your wives with consideration as a delicate vessel, and with honor as fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered.
passages.sermon:
Husbands, live with your wives in an understanding way.
Treat your wives with consideration.
Recognize that your wives are delicate vessels.
Show honor to your wives.
Know that your wives are fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life.
Do these things so that nothing will hinder your prayers.
passages.original: Οἱ ἄνδρες ὁμοίως συνοικοῦντες κατὰ γνῶσιν ὡς ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει τῷ γυναικείῳ ἀπονέμοντες τιμήν ὡς καὶ συνκληρονόμοις χάριτος ζωῆς εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐνκόπτεσθαι τὰς προσευχὰς ὑμῶν

passages.text: Finally, all of you, be like-minded and sympathetic, love as brothers, be tenderhearted and humble.
passages.sermon:
Peter writes to Christians.
He gives instructions for how to live together.
He says, “All of you must be like-minded.”
You must agree with one another.
You must be sympathetic.
You must care about each other’s feelings.
You must love each other as brothers and sisters.
You must be tenderhearted.
You must show compassion.
You must be humble.
You must not think too highly of yourselves.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ τέλος πάντες ὁμόφρονες συμπαθεῖς φιλάδελφοι εὔσπλαγχνοι ταπεινόφρονες

passages.text: Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.
passages.sermon:
God calls you to a new way of living.
Do not repay evil with evil.
Do not repay insult with insult.
Instead, respond with blessing.
God called you to this purpose.
God wants you to inherit a blessing.
passages.original: μὴ ἀποδιδόντες κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἢ λοιδορίαν ἀντὶ λοιδορίας τοὐναντίον δὲ εὐλογοῦντες ὅτι εἰς τοῦτο ἐκλήθητε ἵνα εὐλογίαν κληρονομήσητε

passages.text: For, “Whoever would love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech.
passages.sermon:
This teaching is for anyone who wants to love life.
This person wants to see good days.
He must keep his tongue from evil.
He must not speak deceit with his lips.
passages.original: Ὁ γὰρ θέλων ζωὴν ἀγαπᾶν καὶ ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθὰς παυσάτω τὴν γλῶσσαν ἀπὸ κακοῦ καὶ χείλη τοῦ μὴ λαλῆσαι δόλον

passages.text: He must turn from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.
passages.sermon:
A person must turn away from evil.
A person must do good.
A person must look for peace.
A person must go after peace.
passages.original: ἐκκλινάτω δὲ ἀπὸ κακοῦ καὶ ποιησάτω ἀγαθόν ζητησάτω εἰρήνην καὶ διωξάτω αὐτήν

passages.text: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
passages.sermon: The Lord watches the righteous.\r\nThe Lord listens to the prayers of the righteous.\r\nThe Lord turns His face against those who do evil.
passages.original: ὅτι ὀφθαλμοὶ Κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ εἰς δέησιν αὐτῶν πρόσωπον δὲ Κυρίου ἐπὶ ποιοῦντας κακά

passages.text: Who can harm you if you are zealous for what is good?
passages.sermon:
Peter writes to Christians who suffer for their faith.
He encourages them to do good.
He asks a question.
Who can harm you?
You are zealous for what is good.
God watches over the righteous.
God listens to their prayers.
God stands against those who do evil.
If you are eager to do good, no one can truly harm you.
passages.original: Καὶ τίς ὁ κακώσων ὑμᾶς ἐὰν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ζηλωταὶ γένησθε

passages.text: But even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed. “Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken.”
passages.sermon: If you suffer for doing what is right, you are blessed.\r\nDo not fear what others fear.\r\nDo not let yourself be shaken.
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ εἰ καὶ πάσχοιτε διὰ δικαιοσύνην μακάριοι Τὸν δὲ φόβον αὐτῶν μὴ φοβηθῆτε μηδὲ ταραχθῆτε

passages.text: But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you. But respond with gentleness and respect, keeping a clear conscience, so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.
passages.sermon:
Sanctify Christ as Lord in your hearts.
Always be ready to give an answer to anyone who asks you about your hope.
Speak with gentleness.
Speak with respect.
Keep a good conscience.
Let your good behavior in Christ put to shame those who slander you.
passages.original: Κύριον δὲ τὸν Χριστὸν ἁγιάσατε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν ἕτοιμοι ἀεὶ πρὸς ἀπολογίαν παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντι ὑμᾶς λόγον περὶ τῆς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐλπίδος ἀλλὰ μετὰ πραΰτητος καὶ φόβου συνείδησιν ἔχοντες ἀγαθήν ἵνα ἐν ᾧ καταλαλεῖσθε καταισχυνθῶσιν οἱ ἐπηρεάζοντες ὑμῶν τὴν ἀγαθὴν ἐν Χριστῷ ἀναστροφήν

passages.text: For it is better, if it is God’s will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.
passages.sermon:
God sometimes allows people to suffer.
It is better to suffer for doing good.
It is not good to suffer for doing evil.
If God wills it, choose to do good, even if you must suffer.
Suffering for good is better than suffering for evil.
passages.original: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἀγαθοποιοῦντας εἰ θέλοι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ πάσχειν ἢ κακοποιοῦντας

passages.text: For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit, in whom He also went and preached to the spirits in prison who disobeyed long ago when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In the ark a few people, only eight souls, were saved through water.
passages.sermon:
Christ is righteous.
Christ suffered once for all sins.
He suffered for the unrighteous.
He did this to bring you to God.
People killed Christ in His body.
God made Christ alive in the Spirit.
In the Spirit, Christ went to the spirits in prison.
These spirits had disobeyed long ago.
They disobeyed when God waited patiently.
This happened in the days of Noah.
Noah was building the ark at that time.
Only a few people entered the ark.
Eight people were saved through water.
passages.original: ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἅπαξ περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἔπαθεν δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων ἵνα ὑμᾶς προσαγάγῃ τῷ Θεῷ θανατωθεὶς μὲν σαρκὶ ζωοποιηθεὶς δὲ πνεύματι ἐν ᾧ καὶ τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνεύμασιν πορευθεὶς ἐκήρυξεν ἀπειθήσασίν ποτε ὅτε ἀπεξεδέχετο ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ μακροθυμία ἐν ἡμέραις Νῶε κατασκευαζομένης κιβωτοῦ εἰς ἣν ὀλίγοι τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ὀκτὼ ψυχαί διεσώθησαν δι’ ὕδατος

passages.text: And this water symbolizes the baptism that now saves you also—not the removal of dirt from the body, but the pledge of a clear conscience toward God—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him.
passages.sermon:
Baptism now saves you.
This baptism is not the removal of dirt from the body.
Baptism is the pledge of a good conscience toward God.
God accepts this pledge because of the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ has gone into heaven.
Jesus Christ is at the right hand of God.
All angels, authorities, and powers are subject to Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ὃ καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀντίτυπον νῦν σῴζει βάπτισμα οὐ σαρκὸς ἀπόθεσις ῥύπου ἀλλὰ συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς ἐπερώτημα εἰς Θεόν δι’ ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὅς ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Θεοῦ πορευθεὶς εἰς οὐρανόν ὑποταγέντων αὐτῷ ἀγγέλων καὶ ἐξουσιῶν καὶ δυνάμεων
